diff --git a/inflection/__init__.py b/inflection/__init__.py
index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..fbb0694e6ca149e80563c5d0c27a8faf62838a98 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -360,6 +360,10 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
     create a nicer looking title. :func:`titleize` is meant for creating pretty
     output.
 
+    Words written in capitals, such as acronyms, are kept exactly as they are
+    written.  A string that is written in capitals throughout is not taken to
+    contain acronyms, though: it is capitalized like any other string.
+
     Examples::
 
       >>> titleize("man from the boondocks")
@@ -370,8 +374,100 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       'The Man Without A Past'
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
+      >>> titleize("NASA rocket launch")
+      'NASA Rocket Launch'
+      >>> titleize("the FBI's most_wanted")
+      "The FBI's Most Wanted"
+      >>> titleize("SNAKES ON A PLANE")
+      'Snakes On A Plane'
+
+    """
+    pieces = _split_all_caps(word)
+    last = len(pieces) - 1
+    return ''.join(
+        piece if index % 2 else _titleize_fragment(
+            piece, after_caps=index > 0, before_caps=index < last)
+        for index, piece in enumerate(pieces)
+    )
+
 
+# Finds the all-caps words in a string of character classes made by
+# _char_class(): runs of capital letters, possibly joined by apostrophes (as in
+# DON'T), that are not glued to any other letter.
+_ALL_CAPS_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![Aa])A+(?:'A+)*(?![Aa])")
+
+# Takes the place of an all-caps word while the text next to it is titleized.
+# Like that word it is made of a capital letter, so the text sees the same kind
+# of neighbour (for instance, a digit before it is still split off from it).
+_CAPS_STAND_IN = 'X'
+
+
+def _char_class(char: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Classify a character for :func:`_split_all_caps`: ``'A'`` for a capital
+    letter, ``'a'`` for any other letter, ``"'"`` for an apostrophe and
+    ``'.'`` for anything else.
     """
+    if char.isalpha():
+        return 'A' if char.isupper() else 'a'
+    return "'" if char == "'" else '.'
+
+
+def _split_all_caps(text: str) -> typing.List[str]:
+    """
+    Split ``text`` around the words written in capitals that :func:`titleize`
+    keeps as they are.
+
+    Such a word has two or more capital letters in a row and is set apart from
+    other letters by spaces, punctuation, underscores or digits.  Capitals
+    joined to it by an apostrophe belong to it (``DON'T``), a lowercase ending
+    does not (the ``'s`` of ``NASA's``).  Text without any letters other than
+    capitals, such as ``HELLO WORLD``, is shouting rather than text with
+    acronyms in it, so it is not split at all.
+
+    Like :func:`re.split` with a capturing group, the result alternates
+    between the text around such words (at even indexes, possibly empty) and
+    the words themselves (at odd indexes).
+    """
+    classes = ''.join(map(_char_class, text))
+    if 'a' not in classes:
+        return [text]
+    pieces: typing.List[str] = []
+    end = 0
+    for match in _ALL_CAPS_RE.finditer(classes):
+        if 'AA' in match.group():
+            pieces.append(text[end:match.start()])
+            pieces.append(text[match.start():match.end()])
+            end = match.end()
+    pieces.append(text[end:])
+    return pieces
+
+
+def _titleize_fragment(
+        fragment: str, after_caps: bool, before_caps: bool) -> str:
+    """
+    Titleize ``fragment``, a piece of a longer string that has an all-caps
+    word right before it (``after_caps``) and/or right after it
+    (``before_caps``), the same way it would be titleized as part of the
+    whole string.
+
+    Those neighbours decide how the edges of the fragment are treated: a
+    letter after an apostrophe within a word is lowercased, digits and
+    capitals are split into separate words, a trailing ``"_id"`` is only
+    stripped at the very end of the string, and so on.  Hence a stand-in
+    letter takes their place.  Each stand-in comes out of
+    :func:`_plain_titleize` as exactly one character, which is cut off again.
+    """
+    if not fragment:
+        return fragment
+    head = _CAPS_STAND_IN if after_caps else ''
+    tail = _CAPS_STAND_IN if before_caps else ''
+    titleized = _plain_titleize(head + fragment + tail)
+    return titleized[len(head):len(titleized) - len(tail)]
+
+
+def _plain_titleize(word: str) -> str:
+    """Titleize ``word`` without keeping any all-caps words as they are."""
     return re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),

--- a/test_inflection.py
+++ b/test_inflection.py
@@ -199,6 +199,33 @@ MIXTURE_TO_TITLEIZED: TestParameters = (
     ("Ana Índia",             "Ana Índia"),
 )
 
+ALL_CAPS_WORDS_TO_TITLEIZED: TestParameters = (
+    ('NASA rocket launch',    'NASA Rocket Launch'),
+    ('read the HTTP spec',    'Read The HTTP Spec'),
+    ('launch by NASA',        'Launch By NASA'),
+    ('the FBI and the CIA',   'The FBI And The CIA'),
+    ('HTTP and FTP specs',    'HTTP And FTP Specs'),
+    ('NASA Rocket Launch',    'NASA Rocket Launch'),
+    ('the UK economy',        'The UK Economy'),
+    ("NASA's rocket",         "NASA's Rocket"),
+    ("please DON'T panic",    "Please DON'T Panic"),
+    ('read_the_HTTP_spec',    'Read The HTTP Spec'),
+    ('NASA-led mission',      'NASA Led Mission'),
+    ('the (NASA) mission',    'The (NASA) Mission'),
+    ('MP3 player',            'MP3 Player'),
+    ('2024NASA report',       '2024 NASA Report'),
+    ('author_ID',             'Author ID'),
+    ('ÉCOLE normale',         'ÉCOLE Normale'),
+    ('HTTPServer and NASA',   'Http Server And NASA'),
+    ('  NASA  rocket\tlaunch', '  NASA  Rocket\tLaunch'),
+)
+
+SHOUTING_TO_TITLEIZED: TestParameters = (
+    ('NASA',                  'Nasa'),
+    ('NASA ROCKET LAUNCH',    'Nasa Rocket Launch'),
+    ("DON'T PANIC",           "Don't Panic"),
+)
+
 
 ORDINAL_NUMBERS: TestParameters = (
     ("-1", "-1st"),
@@ -343,6 +370,16 @@ def test_titleize(before: str, titleized: str) -> None:
     assert titleized == inflection.titleize(before)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("before", "titleized"), ALL_CAPS_WORDS_TO_TITLEIZED)
+def test_titleize_keeps_all_caps_words(before: str, titleized: str) -> None:
+    assert titleized == inflection.titleize(before)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("before", "titleized"), SHOUTING_TO_TITLEIZED)
+def test_titleize_capitalizes_shouting(before: str, titleized: str) -> None:
+    assert titleized == inflection.titleize(before)
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize(("camel", "underscore"), CAMEL_TO_UNDERSCORE)
 def test_camelize(camel: str, underscore: str) -> None:
     assert camel == inflection.camelize(underscore)
description: titleize splits the input around standalone all-caps words (Unicode-aware, apostrophe-joined like DON'T, found with a character-class regex), emits them verbatim and runs the original algorithm on the text between them with a capital stand-in letter for each neighbouring word so edge rules (apostrophes, digit splits, trailing _id) are unchanged; input with no non-capital letters is treated as shouting and titleized as before
